events.title: U.S. judge rules Microsoft violated antitrust law
events.summary: On April 3, 2000, U.S. District Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson ruled that [Microsoft] had violated [antitrust] laws by maintaining a monopoly through anti-competitive conduct — during the same month the dot-com bubble began to burst.
events.about: The findings targeted browser bundling and [OEM] restrictions that had kneecapped [Netscape]. Jackson later ordered a breakup (later reversed on appeal), but the case forced [Microsoft] to open APIs, document protocols, and accept oversight — influencing how regulators later treated Google, Apple, and Amazon.

narrative.whyChosen: The ruling was the defining [antitrust] moment of the [PC] software era.
narrative.whyImportant: It constrained how platform owners could bundle products and exclude rivals.
narrative.problemSolved: Competitors argued Windows integration made independent browsers and [middleware] impossible to sell.
